title: Understanding the Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The expected squared error can be broken down into three components: variance, bias squared, and irreducible error. Can you identify which part of the equation corresponds to each component?

title: Identifying the Components
text: In the equation E[(Y-f_hat_theta(x))**2]=sigma**2+(h(x)-E[f_hat_theta(x)])**2+E[(E[f_hat_theta(x)]-f_hat_theta(x))**2], which term represents the variance?

title: Variance Component
text: The variance component is the expected value of the squared difference between the expected prediction and the actual prediction. Which term in the equation represents this?

title: Bias Component
text: Which term in the equation represents the bias squared?

title: Bias Squared Component
text: The bias squared component is the squared difference between the true function and the expected prediction. Which term in the equation represents this?

title: Irreducible Error
text: What is the irreducible error in the equation?

title: Irreducible Error Component
text: The irreducible error is the variance of the noise in the data. Which term in the equation represents this?
